submitted.rationale: Index 89 (Ca0.21 Cu0.39 V0.40, Cu:V ≈ 1:1, likely a Cu2V2O7-type vanadate) gave the highest measured EQE, 0.213%. The other two measurements were lower: 0.166% for the Cu-rich index 134 and 0.106% for the more V-rich index 69. Among the samples measured, EQE peaks near Cu:V = 1.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.166%, lower than 89; excess Cu reduces merit.
Measured EQE 0.106%; moving toward V-rich lowered merit.
Not measured. MEGNet gives V2O5 an HSE gap of 2.83 eV, above 2.4 eV, so it should absorb weakly, and the measured trend falls off toward V.

consultations.verdict: V2O5 is stable (e_hull 0) but has a predicted HSE gap of 2.83 eV, which is above the 2.4 eV photon energy. So the V-rich corner should absorb weakly. Cu vanadates have smaller gaps (~2 eV), so a Cu-rich composition is favored. This supports measuring 134 (the highest-Cu corner).

The two fidelities disagree on the V2O5 gap: GLLB gives 2.15 eV and HSE gives 2.83 eV. So some V-rich absorption at 2.4 eV is possible, but the result is only weakly informative. I'm testing a Cu:V ≈ 1:1 (Cu2V2O7-like) composition at index 89 to get a second point between the Cu-rich corner and the V-rich region. The result is uninformative on its own; this is an exploration choice.

SCAN gives a V2O5 gap of 1.77 eV, below 2.4 eV, so it doesn't penalize adding more vanadium. That mildly supports continuing the measured trend: EQE rose from 0.166 at Cu 0.54 to 0.213 at Cu 0.39/V 0.40. Index 69 (Cu 0.30, V 0.50, low Ca) takes one more step along that trend.
